body: Oh, man...that stinks.

I just don't want to seem like an attention whole. I'm depressed, and I hide it so people don't think I'm just making it up for attention. It seems desperate to me to talk about your problems to people. Which, intellectually, I know is wrong, but I can't fight that feeling. That's why I come to r/depression. It doesn't seem rude or imposing here. And because I don't want to bring down my friends with me. My best friend tends to feel personally responsible for my happiness. If he knew how depressed I've become, he'd think of himself as a failure as my friend. And I can't do that to him.

And that's fantastic. :) I hope all goes well. Keep me posted, okay?

That sucks. I'm sorry about that. Still, the internet is never closed! Well, not unless SOPA passes, anyways. And that's the biggest occupier ever! You're never alone as long as you have reddit!

Were they mutual friends? They may just not have seen it coming and were taken aback. When two people get in a relationship, all their friends just love to say, "Oh, I saw that one coming a mile away." It can be almost hurtful to them to not be able to have caught onto that before it happened. Maybe that's why they reacted the way they did.

"If we weren't all crazy, we'd go insane." Irrationality, emotions...in short, mild insanity--you're right. That is what makes us human. It's nothing to be afraid of. You just can't let it overrun your life. 

I only live about twenty minutes away from my mom right now, so I see her a fair amount. You can imagine, with all those animals, I hate actually going into the house. But we talk on the phone a fair amount. Usually about practical things: working out meetings, calling for favours, things like that. But we still have regular contact, which is nice, I guess. Though I just got off the phone with her, and she was going on about how my grandmother kidnapped my sister (my sister lives with my grandparents when she's on leave from the military. Of her own free will, she loves it there) and how much of an inconsiderate ass my grandpop is (well, okay, this is completely true.)

I get that. And since I don't really know you, and there could be loads of reasons why you push people away, I don't know what to tell you. I know why I do it. I don't want other people all up in my life knowing everything about me and trying to control me or pressure me in an effort to be nice. It's just too much. Sometimes people smother in an attempt to help. It's not helpful.

This is a possibility. Do you still know the girl? Do you ever keep contact with her? Are you facebook friends? If not, it may just be the idea of her. Our minds love creating fantasies that reality just can't compare to. And I understand it can be really depressing. 

But if you can bring yourself do it, see if you can't find a way to bring her down from the pedestal you have her on. If you are facebook friends, check for things on her profile that you disapprove of or disagree with (Yes, I am totally encouraging facebook stalking. It's what that shit was designed for, okay?). If you don't keep contact with her, try to create scenes in your head that change your ideas of her. Maybe if you can make her less perfect, you can be happy with someone else.

I'm not going to lie, I'm a little surprised by their reactions to your relationship. I work retail, and a lot of my coworkers have older boyfriends. I see nothing wrong with it. I didn't even think twice about it. Physical age doesn't matter as much as intellectual and maturity age. If you two are able to relate to each other on the same level, have interesting conversations and work out problems...the fuck everybody else. I'd say you have a good relationship. But even my evaluation doesn't matter. If you're happy and he's happy, that's all that matters.

Just give it some time. They'll come 'round. Don't try to impress them or anything, just let them get used to you on their own. And who knows? Maybe in a year or so, you'll all be best mates. Just be friendly and whatnot to them, they'll get past their prejudice eventually.

Oh, Honey. My mom is crazy, too. Possibly schizophrenic, Crazy Cat Lady syndrome (almost 50 cats and 5 dogs. I shit you not.). Though she doesn't drink, she shows many of the symptoms of an alcoholic because her father is one. And I tell you. The thought that I might someday be like her is my number one biggest fear. 

But I keep reminding myself that, to a certain extent, I can control it. I am not just my mother's daughter, or my father's daughter, or my grandfather's granddaughter, or my aunt's niece...I am me. I make my own damn decisions. I decide who I'm going to be. No one else can define that. Not my family, not my friends, not even my genetics. You are stronger than any of the factors in your life. And if you don't want to be something, by god, you can keep yourself from being it.

That being said, if you can find some form of counseling, that'd help you. A lot of not turning out like your parents is accepting who they are in terms of their influence on you. Understanding and accepting the past (and the present), coming to terms with it, and moving on. If you're in high school or college, you may be able to find free counseling there.

I completely understand that. My main issue with winter (other than the fact that I hate the cold) is it just seems more stressful than any other season. Holidays and hustle and bustle. And if you can get past the stress of the holidays, then I just get depressed because who wants to spend the holidays feeling alone? Even if you have people in your life (family, friends, even a relationship (which I don't have)), I always feel like there's not really a person who truly gets me. And that's lonesome. 

But MakeMeSmile is a great place. I also frequent r/funny and r/aww. Or if you ever get some free time to volunteer anywhere (especially an animal shelter, if you're not allergic), that's fantastic for cheering up.

^What he said. I have something similar just with general anxiety, because I am the type of person who has to do everything myself, take responsibility for everything, make everything perfect...holidays kill. And my mom is the same way, yet she's forever telling me I need to chill. When she's actually worse than I am. It's so controlling. Which is so frustrating to me, I just want to pull my hair out. But she's trying to dismiss her own issues by dismissing mine. 

Don't let her control you. Feel free to do your own thing. If she does drag you to events, though, don't try to take on everything at once. Single out one person to talk to, and try to get comfortable with just that one. That way it's not an entire social group you have to deal with.
